recommended_title: Risk-Adaptive Frozen-Score Controls: Conditional Gains and Limits for Mean Inference
central_question: With labels, unlabeled observations, and a scalar predictor fixed within each repeated-sampling comparison, when does training-only cross-fitted score calibration shorten mean confidence intervals relative to label-only inference, PPI, and PPI++, and what does the evidence establish about coverage?
central_thesis: The frozen risk-adaptive control method yields narrower mean intervals than PPI and PPI++ on the evaluated empirical gene-expression source, but is wider than PPI++ in all six synthetic or perturbed-score conditions; observed coverage and offset-invariant studentization support a conditional efficiency study, not universal narrowing or a finite-sample validity certificate.
narrative_rationale: One shared question connects the real scalar table, synthetic conditions, and score perturbations. The completed final evaluation supplies 400 paired repeats per condition, interval endpoints, baseline coverage, and stored uncertainty summaries. A direct condition-by-comparator view is scientifically stronger than a search-score story: the selected method has aggregate coverage 0.9610714285714286, minimum condition coverage 0.95, and a reported capped mean episode width ratio of 1.2106794607646876. The gene-expression paired width-difference interval versus PPI++ is [-0.02969064263718976, -0.02435572792761422], whereas the corresponding differences are positive in the other six conditions. Qualification is completed/qualified/true in final.qualification.*, independently of the absent downstream_study. The conservative scientific_validity field is explicitly fixed to zero by the local evaluator, so it is neither evidence of an identified validity failure nor a certificate. Theoretical headroom and offset invariance explain the design space, not the measured cause of the real-table gain. No component ablation identifies that cause.

method_groups.name: Label-only mean intervals
method_groups.include_reason: The matched reference uses exact binomial Clopper-Pearson intervals for binary outcomes and Student-t intervals for real outcomes. It isolates whether a frozen score adds practical value; Student-t is not distribution-free exact for the empirical real source.

method_groups.name: PPI and PPI++ mean intervals
method_groups.include_reason: Both were evaluated on identical inputs using ppi-python 0.2.3, with coefficient 1 and its optimized coefficient respectively. Keep them distinct: the original comparator remains scientifically relevant, and the optimized reference is essential to reveal the six conditions without a width benefit. Their asymptotic status and rare-event behavior must accompany width comparisons.

method_groups.name: Risk-adaptive cross-fitted frozen-score controls
method_groups.include_reason: This is the frozen selection with final evidence: nested training-only zero/affine/spline calibration, finite-unlabeled-sample multiplier, weighted held-out residuals, and a shared-pool variance computed after combining controls. Report its t-based return path and label-only fallbacks, not its separate unreturned certificate.

method_groups.name: Constant-score and permuted-score perturbations
method_groups.include_reason: They reuse the nonlinear records under specified score transformations and test dependence on score information without changing the method. Present alongside the independently uninformative condition; do not call them isolated ablations of calibration or variance estimation.

results_focus: Primary: all seven final conditions, each with the frozen method and all three matched comparators; foreground paired width differences or ratios of mean widths together with per-method coverage uncertainty. Never select only the favorable real source.

Gene-expression empirical source: mean widths are 0.4488074070562893 for the frozen method, 0.4759006085515874 for PPI++, 0.4727476605089987 for PPI, and 1.5263806745747615 for label-only inference. Candidate coverage is 0.9575, with stored simultaneous interval [0.9163118126035984, 0.9824159148164467]. This is resampling from the frozen empirical source, not external biological-population validation.

Boundary of benefit: every other condition has a positive paired mean-width difference versus PPI++; the nonlinear condition itself does not show a benefit. Distinguish improvement relative to label-only or unoptimized PPI from improvement relative to PPI++.

Coverage: show the 0.95 target and stored simultaneous Clopper-Pearson intervals across seven conditions and four methods. The frozen method's observed condition coverage spans 0.95 to 0.98, but its lower uncertainty bounds do not establish coverage at or above 0.95.

Rare outcomes: PPI++ observed coverage is 0.92 and its stored interval is [0.868958106205729, 0.9562534828761202], which still includes 0.95. Five of its 400 intervals have zero width. Retain its width evidence with these caveats rather than treating narrower intervals as automatically valid or declaring a statistically established coverage failure.

Metric audit: the reported aggregate width ratio averages capped per-episode ratios and assigns 100 to a positive candidate width over a zero-width reference. Use paired absolute differences and ratios of means for scientific interpretation; distinguish these estimands explicitly and retain the original aggregate only as a documented secondary result.

Mechanistic scope: deterministic-control finite-N variance/headroom identities and fold-offset invariance are explanatory algebra. Overlapping fitted folds, heuristic family selection, critical-value differences, clipping, and fallbacks prevent attributing the measured width change to one component without unavailable controlled ablations.
